claims.claim: Let D(m,n) be the maximum push number of a sortable m×n instance, N=mn, s=min{m,n}, and t=max{m,n}. Then D(m,n)=O(N·min{s,log t}).
claims.evidence: Assume 2≤m=s≤n=t and transpose to a p×q board with p=n and q=m, relabeling each target position accordingly. The FillColumns proof remains valid without p≤q: each column rotates at most p−1 times, and while f columns are underfull, every q buffer-row rotations reduce the wrong-body potential by at least f/2. Each of O(log q) phases therefore contains O(p) such blocks, for O(pq log q)=O(N log s) pushes. FloatMinimums and Claim 5 then give every transposed column its exact target-token set, so after transposition every original row has its target-token set. An even within-row permutation is implemented by two equal-size involutions whose opposite SwapPairs side effects cancel. Odd permutations are reduced by one row rotation when n is even; when n is odd and m is even, the residual auxiliary-body cycle is even and is reversed by two transposed involution calls. On odd-by-odd boards, global parity makes the number of odd rows even, and exact adjacent-row double-swap gadgets pair their residual transpositions. Each row costs O(N), so this gives O(Ns). Taking the better of this construction and the source's O(N log t) algorithm proves the claim. One-dimensional cases are immediate.
claims.search_method: Dimension-independent potential analysis, permutation-parity case analysis, and exact simulation of SwapPairs, transposed repairs, and odd-by-odd pairing gadgets.

claims.claim: For every fixed s≥2, boards with min{m,n}=s have asymptotically tight push number D(m,n)=Θ(mn).
claims.evidence: Claim 0 gives D(s,t)=O(st·s)=O(st) for each fixed s. Translating the sorted board by floor(t/2) columns and floor(s/2) rows has, by Claim 2, exact distance s·floor(t/2)+t·floor(s/2)=Ω(st) as t tends to infinity. Thus the upper and lower bounds match at Θ(mn).
claims.witness: For dimensions s×t, the half-translated sorted board has exact distance s·floor(t/2)+t·floor(s/2).
claims.search_method: Deduction from the verified upper bound and the displacement-certified translation family, supplemented by exact small-board BFS checks.

claims.claim: Every instance A has the displacement certificate pn(A)≥ceil(H(A)/n)+ceil(V(A)/m). Moreover, a global translation by a columns and b rows has exact push number m·d_n(a)+n·d_m(b), where d_k(z)=min(z mod k,k−(z mod k)).
claims.evidence: With H and V the sums, over tokens, of shortest cyclic horizontal and vertical distances to their targets, one row push changes H by at most n and leaves V unchanged, while one column push changes V by at most m and leaves H unchanged. Hence every sorting word contains at least ceil(H/n) row pushes and ceil(V/m) column pushes, and the bounds add; unsortable instances may consistently be assigned pn=∞. For a global (a,b)-translation, H=mn·d_n(a) and V=mn·d_m(b), giving the stated lower bound. Rotating each of the m rows back d_n(a) times and each of the n columns back d_m(b) times attains it exactly.
claims.witness: The global (a,b)-translation has a matching word consisting of m·d_n(a) row pushes and n·d_m(b) column pushes.
claims.search_method: A 1-Lipschitz displacement-potential proof plus exhaustive exact checks over the reachable states of 2×2, 2×3, 2×4, and 3×3 boards.

claims.claim: A sharper general counting lower bound is D(m,n)≥ceil(log_{d−1}(1+(d−2)(Q−1)/d)), where d=2(m+n), Q=(mn)! if m or n is even, and Q=(mn)!/2 otherwise.
claims.evidence: The sortable component has exactly Q states by the parity characterization. A geodesic cannot contain a generator immediately followed by its inverse, so at most 1+d·((d−1)^L−1)/(d−2) endpoints are represented by words of length at most L. Coincident generators on dimension-two boards only make this an overcount. Taking L=D, requiring this quantity to cover Q, and rearranging gives (d−1)^D≥1+(d−2)(Q−1)/d; integrality of D yields the displayed ceiling. The checker evaluated the ceiling solely by integer powers and cross-multiplication.
claims.search_method: Exact non-backtracking Cayley-ball count, algebraic rearrangement, and integer-only comparison with small-board exact diameters.

claims.claim: Global translations are not generally diametral: D(2,3)=7, whereas every translated 2×3 board has distance at most 5.
claims.evidence: Exact BFS using the seven distinct 2×3 unit generators reached all 720 configurations with level sizes [1,7,31,115,274,253,36,3], proving diameter 7. The stated seven-push word reaches ((3,2,1),(6,5,4)), and BFS assigns that state distance 7. The six global translations have exact distances [0,2,2,3,5,5], so their maximum is 5.
claims.witness: Starting from ((1,2,3),(4,5,6)), the word R1-left, C1-up, R1-left, C1-up, C3-up, R1-right, C1-up reaches ((3,2,1),(6,5,4)), whose exact BFS distance is 7.
claims.search_method: Complete exact-arithmetic breadth-first search of the 2×3 Cayley graph and exhaustive enumeration of all six translations.

claims.claim: Given a p×q matrix in which every column is body-full, its buffer row can be sorted in O(pq) pushes while preserving the set of tokens in every column body.
claims.evidence: Under the source's standing p,q≥2 convention, body-fullness leaves exactly the q buffer tokens in the heads. For an even required head permutation π, write π=συ with σ and υ involutions having the same number k of transpositions. Literal analysis of SwapPairs shows that applying σ and υ with opposite side-effect directions permutes the heads as required and applies inverse cyclic shifts to the same k bodies, restoring them. For odd π, write π=συτ; the first two calls cancel as before, and the final transposition shifts one body cyclically without changing its token set. Since k≤q/2, the total cost is O(kp+q)+O(p+q)=O(pq). Exact simulations checked every head permutation for q=2,…,6 and p=2,…,5, totaling 3,488 cases.
claims.search_method: Permutation decomposition proof and literal exact simulation of all three SwapPairs phases across 3,488 cleanup instances.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for asymptotically tight bounds in the general m×n regime, closing the full multiplicative Θ(log max{m,n}) gap. The verified O(N·min{s,log t}) upper bound and fixed-s Θ(N) classification are material improvements, but when s≥log t the draft still supplies only the general Ω(N) lower bound against O(N log t). It therefore does not close the requested general gap. The draft labels itself PARTIAL and explicitly states this limitation, so its claimed resolution is accurate and its final writeup does not overclaim target coverage.
